# Sources — every primary document downloaded for this project

**Generated by `sources/build-sources-inventory.py`. Do not hand-edit.**
Run `python3 sources/build-sources-inventory.py` to rebuild, or `check` to detect drift.

This lists what is **held locally in `/sources`** — the documents the project’s
figures are derived from and can be re-checked against. It is not the citation list:
`files/CITATIONS.md` maps every number on screen to its source, and is generated from
the tools themselves. This file answers the prior question — what is actually on disk.

Derived outputs (the `.csv` and `.json` each script writes) are listed per folder but
kept separate: they are this project’s own work, not downloaded evidence.

## One qualification, stated up front

**The DOE LEAD archives are not all held here.** `lead-harvest.py` downloads one
state at a time from `data.openei.org`, derives the burden and bill figures, and
**deletes the archive** — New Mexico’s alone is 54 MB and the full set across 51
jurisdictions runs to several gigabytes. What is kept is New Mexico’s raw archive as a
worked example, the derived CSVs for all 51, and the script that reproduces them from
a documented URL pattern.

So for household burden, re-checking the other 50 jurisdictions means re-running the
harvest against openei.org rather than reading a file in this folder. Every other
dataset below **is** held locally and its scripts run offline.
